newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL PUT WORLD RECORD $150 MILLION TAG ON MIJATOVIC.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL PUT WORLD RECORD $150 MILLION TAG ON MIJATOVIC.

text.p: Predrag Mijatovic signed a new contract with Real Madrid on Friday by which any club wanting to buy the Montenegrin striker would have to pay the Spanish champions a world record $150 million.
The deal will keep Mijatovic at the club until 2003.
On Wednesday Real had already created a record for a 'withdrawal clause' by putting a price of $100 million on Brazilian defender Roberto Carlos.
"I'm the new record holder but I'm sure it won't be for long," Mijatovic said.
Meanwhile Real goalkeeper Bodo Illgner denied that he was unhappy at the Madrid side.
"It seems strange and serious to me that everybody should say I will not stay in Real Madrid...I'm happy here." Illgner said.
Recent media reports suggested the rest of the Real squad were unhappy that the German international had missed all the team's celebrations after securing the Spanish title.
He was also rumoured to be following coach Fabio Capello to AC Milan.
Illgner was brought to Spain from Cologne because Capello felt the team needed a taller goalkeeper.
